problems.explain: The probability is 92%, which is 23/25. On the scale from 0 (impossible) to 1 (certain), it is above 3/4, so closer to 1 than to 1/2. (Likely is not certain: it can still fail to happen.) So likely.

prompt.v: The table shows the results of 48 rolls of a number cube. If the experiment is repeated for many more trials, about what will the experimental probability of rolling a 5 most likely be?

problems.explain: Over more and more trials the share of 5s settles toward the theoretical 1/6, which over 48 is 8/48: the luck of a short run averages out. (It does not have to "catch up" by going past 8/48 the other way, and 15/48 was one short run, not the truth: each roll is still 1/6.) So about 8/48.

prompt.v: First a spinner with 4 equal sections, numbered 1 to 4, is spun, then a coin is flipped. Which list is the sample space? (1T means 1, then tails.)

problems.text: sample list: 1 2 3 4 x H T; options a=1H 1H 2H 2T 3H 3T 4H 4T, b=1H 1T, c=1H 1H, d=1H 1T 2H 2T 3H 3T 4H 4T
problems.explain: Each of the 4 first outcomes goes with every one of the 2 second outcomes, so the sample space has 4 × 2 = 8 outcomes, each once: 1H, 1T, 2H, 2T, 3H, 3T, 4H, 4T. (A list of only the outcomes that start with 1, or one that repeats an outcome in place of another, is not the sample space.) So 1H, 1T, 2H, 2T, 3H, 3T, 4H, 4T.
